correctness.rationale: The graph is explicitly constructed by poles, pentagonal rings and cross-ring edges; its degree five and isomorphism to the standard icosahedral graph are checked. The exact local rule is the threshold of three of five neighbors. Independent source programs use different graph encodings and independent bit-count versus triple-conjunction threshold computations and exhaust all 4096 labelled states, reproducing the complete first-entry/period table, exact fixed set, orbit and basin counts. The direct trajectory 87,47,23,41,16,0 proves sharpness of first entry time five, and the exhaustive test F^7=F^5 proves all-state entrance by five. Every graph automorphism is enumerated through an exhaustive adjacency/nonadjacency backtrack, yielding exactly 120; applying them to the 156 normalized two-cycles yields seven classes. Neither incomplete sampling nor simulation extrapolation is used. The program input files are embedded and can be independently recompiled.

evidence: Goles–Olivos (1980) prove eventual period at most two on finite symmetric binary threshold networks. Benjamini et al., arXiv:1405.2486v1, discuss finite period two and prove infinite/random-network results. Kaaser–Mallmann-Trenn–Natale (2016) give general voting-time upper bounds and asymmetry reductions, not an exact twelve-site phase portrait. The existing dodecahedral-majority result, identifier 095dfb0decea, concerns a degree-three twenty-vertex graph.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The classical stronger-in-scope period theorem covers possible period lengths but does not imply the numerical orbit, basin or geometric class counts. The dual dodecahedral graph has a nonisomorphic adjacency structure and majority threshold two rather than three, so its exact result does not dominate the present claim.

value.rationale: The icosahedral graph is a distinguished Platonic five-regular network with a 120-element symmetry group and six antipodal vertex pairs. Exact basin accessibility is independently motivated by the difference between geometric stability and dynamical attraction: although twelve nonconstant fixed supports exist, every one is isolated with a singleton basin. Meanwhile two unanimous fixed points each attract 1586 states, and exactly 156 genuine two-cycles exhibit four basin sizes and seven symmetry classes. The sharp five-update entry distribution gives a complete nontrivial phase portrait, rather than a generic period-two observation, an arbitrary parameter slice or a known-table recomputation. Future comparisons with other polyhedral or highly symmetric odd-degree graphs can use the exact census. No family theorem or unproved generality is claimed.
